title: codemod-split-engine --members: move registerApp, registerDriver and registerHook out of the landed engine.ts facade (hand-edited engine-registration.ts header; registerHook's undo proof fails at the import block)
body:
domain:server#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CYVV6fcAQrNTDQRvPb

Filing gate: ① tooling gap found by the #30054 dev (PR #30571, os-dev-report 6663232806). Confirmed by the seat from the PR's readings. ⛔ Not a claim. Suggested grade: p3.

## What happens

#30054's `engine.ts` half (PR #30571) spells the return types of eight `ObjectQL` facade methods, with the public `.d.ts` byte-equal, and moves five of them into their facets with #30055's `--members` pass. Three bodies would not move:

- `registerApp` and `registerDriver`: `--members` refuses with "engine-registration.ts: its header is not as the first pass wrote it". That module's header was edited by hand when `isExternalWriteForbidden` was written there (#30370).
- `registerHook`: `--members` writes the move, but its undo proof fails: "undoing the moves out of engine-hooks-and-functions.ts does not rebuild its base (first difference at line 44)", in that module's import block.

Each was measured alone and together. Their three rows stay in `scripts/facade-delegation-registry.json` (card `#30054`) with a reason naming the refusal.

## Ask

Teach `scripts/codemod-split-engine.mjs --members` to accept a facet module whose header carries hand-written members, and to prove an undo when the moved body changes the module's import block, without weakening the byte-for-byte undo proof. Then move the three bodies and drop their registry rows.

Reader: the facade tooling owner (`scripts/codemod-split-engine.mjs`, `scripts/check-facade-delegation-only.mjs`). Links: #30054, PR #30571, #30055, #30370, #30518 (the protocol.ts sibling).
